summary: Iteration 121: isolated QA of the owner-only verified JEE transfer importer (tejas/jee_transfer.py + pinned resources/jee_chapters.json.gz + JeeTransferPanel). All checks ran against the dedicated DB tejas_isolated_iter105_test, using MOCKED auth (X-Test-User override of auth.current; the real staff/owner deps still ran) and MOCKED storage (in-memory GET-only mock plus a TEST-ONLY hash shim that maps only the mock PDF bytes to the expected SHA, so the real verify_pdf size, %PDF- and hash comparisons run unchanged). Real storage was blocked by a guard. No production calls, no LLM, and no customer-DB writes. A read-only probe showed the customer preview DB unchanged before and after: 222 sets, 6 books, 134 files, 1 user, 1 attempt, no receipt. BACKEND pytest: 33/33 passed twice, no flakes. Coverage: (1) the bundle's uncompressed SHA matches 3551e344…; 81 files, 3 books and 78 sets (Physics 29, Mathematics 26, Chemistry 23); 3900 unique questions, each with a supplied_worked solution and q_refs/s_refs; timers 90/120/70 with +4/-1/0; per-record hashes match record_sha256; independent_audit PASS; a tampered bundle gives 503; the bundle is not routed (on the public URL these paths return the SPA HTML or a 404 JSON, never the gzip). (2) Role matrix on GET and POST: anonymous 401, student 403, reviewer 403, unverified-phone owner 403, owner 200. Strict EmptyPayload returns 422 for dict, list, string and number bodies, and an oversized body is rejected, all with no receipt and no storage calls. (3) GET status x3 changed nothing (full DB snapshot equal, zero storage calls). (4) Size, header and hash mismatches give 409, StorageError gives 503 and timeout gives 503. All leave verified_files=0, release the lease and insert nothing. Storage GETs follow the exact bundle path order. No target record is inserted until 81/81 PDFs are verified. Interrupt and resume work from verified_files 40. Two concurrent steps give one 200 and one 409. A stale lease blocks until expiry (clock +301s). A second owner id gets 409. A changed unrelated set blocks the switch to the import phase with 409 and no progress, then continues once reverted. (5) Import: a simulated crash after insert but before the receipt update deduplicates on retry. A conflicting record with a target ID appearing mid-run gives 409 without overwriting, and the cursor stays at 96. Completion gives 81/3/78 exactly, and every stored record digest equals the target. The only differences from the bundle are books.created_by and sets.rights_attested_by, both remapped to the owner. Null fields are preserved, all 3900 question hashes match, there are no duplicate IDs, and unrelated files/books/sets/users/attempts/sessions are byte-identical. A repeat step after completion is a no-op (no writes, no storage calls). The catalogue shows 29/26/23 chapters at 90/120/70 min. A pre-existing different target record gives 409 before any receipt or storage call. (6) Read-only probe of the preview DB: all 162 target records already exist there and are digest-identical for the current preview owner id edc17534… (proves the Mongo round-trip digest is stable), and content() parses every existing doc. FRONTEND (real Studio page, /api routed via Playwright route.fetch to a TEST-ONLY bridge on 127.0.0.1:8767, session mocked): the GET-status failure shows jee-transfer-error and jee-transfer-retry, and retry recovers. There are 0 step calls on mount and remount. Title, scope, environment (shows the current hostname) and safety copy render. Start shows progress and the pause button, and pause stops the loop after the current step (step count stable). The label becomes 'Resume verified import'. A hash-failure 409 shows the error, and resume clears it and continues. Navigating away (unmount) produced no further steps within 3s of the check. Resume ran to 'Import complete': 81/81, 162/162, 78/78, progress bar 243/243, button disabled. Reviewer sees no panel and student is redirected to /owner-login, with zero jee-transfer calls from either. Overflow is 0px at 1920x800 and 390x844. The bridge was killed, the isolated DB dropped and the /tmp control files removed. PRODUCTION is NOT modified; real-PDF/storage and real-auth production proof is still pending.

minor.issue: Partial publication: sets are inserted directly with status 'published' in 8-record batches. The batch at cursor 80 mixes the last file, the 3 books and sets 84-87. If an import stops part-way (conflict, outage or the owner pausing), students immediately see a partial chapter catalogue until it is resumed. The target_policy says 'Stage private ... then publish only these sets', so staged-then-flip would match the policy more closely. Safe for data, but not atomic across collections.

The receipt is bound to the first owner_id. A different owner id gets 409 'Another owner import step is running' permanently, which is a misleading message and leaves no way forward if the owner account id ever differs.

On timeout, asyncio.wait_for(to_thread(verify_pdf)) stops waiting, but the storage thread keeps running (up to 3x120s retries). The lease is released, so repeated resumes can stack background GET threads. Low impact.

Each step deep-copies the whole bundle (target_records) and lru_cache keeps the decompressed bundle in process memory. Acceptable for about 100 steps (the full isolated run took about 10s), noted for memory.

issues: Uses a native <progress> (default green and grey track) instead of the design-system/shadcn Progress, so it looks inconsistent with the app's maroon theme
The text 'Preview imports do not update your live site' is static, so it also appears on the production hostname; consider wording conditional on environment
The jee-transfer-retry button exists only for a failed initial GET; after a failed step the Resume button acts as retry (works, but a labelled 'Retry' would be clearer)

action_items: Optional: stage the 78 sets privately (or publish in a final dedicated step) so a stopped import never exposes a partial catalogue; otherwise document the partial-visibility semantics for the owner
Optional: give a clear message or recovery path when the receipt's owner_id differs from the current owner
Optional: replace the native <progress> with the shadcn Progress component; make the preview/live wording depend on the environment
Operational: production import still needs a real owner run after the code-only redeploy (real 81-PDF storage GETs are not covered by QA)
critical_code_review_comments: Ordered batches: 0-80 files, 81-83 books, 84-161 sets. inventory and verify_baseline run before the first set batch (cursor 80) and at completion, but not in other batches; append_record still checks each record against conflicts.
Resume semantics confirmed: the cursor persists only after a whole batch succeeds. A failed or crashed batch re-runs and identical records are skipped.

content() requires an 'id' on every document in tejas_files, tejas_chapter_books and tejas_sets (baseline_snapshot iterates over all of them). This holds in preview (0 docs without an id) but was not verified for production; a legacy doc without an id would cause a 500 on the first step.
Running the import in preview would make 81 real storage GETs and write a receipt into the preview DB, while all 162 records would be skipped as identical.
